title: Startup dependency check with fast-fail
description:
Check all required external dependencies at startup and fail fast with a clear, actionable error message if any are unavailable.

Why this issue exists:
Currently the daemons start successfully and then fail on the first operation that needs Kubo. The error appears deep in a stack trace on the first article write, not at startup. Operators need to know immediately at launch if the environment is misconfigured.

Scope:
On startup, before binding the listen port, check:
- Kubo reachable: GET /api/v0/id succeeds and returns a peer ID
- SQLite databases openable and migrations runnable
- TLS cert and key files readable and parseable (if TLS is configured)
- Signing key file readable and correct length (if signing_key_path is configured)
- Admin bind address not already in use

On any check failure:
- Log the specific failure at ERROR with an actionable message ('Kubo unreachable at http://127.0.0.1:5001 -- is ipfs daemon running?')
- Exit with code 1 before binding any ports
- Do not partially start (no half-bound sockets left behind)

Add a --check flag that runs the dependency checks and exits without starting the daemon. Useful for config validation in CI and deployment scripts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Starting with Kubo down: process exits within 5 seconds with exit code 1 and a clear error naming Kubo
- Starting with a bad TLS cert path: exits with exit code 1 naming the file
- --check flag exits 0 when all checks pass, 1 with errors listed when any fail
- Normal startup with all deps available is not measurably slower
